title: A free-free beam's first frequency
model: a 200 x 10 x 10 mm steel beam (E 210 GPa, 7850 kg/m^3) with no support (free: true); 2.5 mm elements

f1.source: Euler-Bernoulli, free-free: f = (4.7300^2 / 2 pi L^2) sqrt(E I / (rho A)) (Blevins, Formulas for Natural Frequency and Mode Shape, 1979, table 8-1, the free-free beam)
f1.reason: Euler-Bernoulli leaves out shear and rotary inertia, which at L/h = 20 lower a free-free beam's first frequency by about one percent; the mesh error at 2.5 mm is under 0.1 %. The six rigid modes are set apart and labelled rigid, their Rayleigh quotients zero to rounding (under 0.003 Hz here); CalculiX is not run (a modal study is in-house)
